'''Jesús Ildefonso Díaz''' is a Spanish [[mathematician]] who works in [[partial differential equation]]s. He is a professor at [[Complutense University of Madrid]] (UCM)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cica.udc.es/en/event/119|title=Conferencia Jesús Ildefonso Díaz Díaz: "Matemáticas para el Nanomundo" - Event|website=cica.udc.es|access-date=2019-05-07|archive-date=2019-05-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190507215915/https://cica.udc.es/en/event/119|url-status=dead}}</ref> and a member of the [[Spanish Royal Academy of Sciences]].

== Biography ==
Díaz was born in Toledo, Spain on December 11, 1950.<ref name=":0" /> He graduated in mathematics from UCM in 1973, and obtained his PhD from the same university in 1976. His Ph.D. thesis advisors were Alberto Dou and [[Haïm Brezis]].

== Career ==
Díaz joined the faculty at UCM as an Associate Professor in Mathematical Analysis in 1978.  He moved briefly to the [[University of Santander]] in 1980, before returning to UCM as a full professor in 1983. In 1998, he co-founded the journal ''Revista Matemática de la UCM'' and served on its editorial board from 1988 to 1995.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mat.ucm.es/serv/revista/p_board.htm|title=RMC - Editorial staff|website=www.mat.ucm.es|access-date=2019-07-22}}</ref>  He founded the Department of Applied Mathematics at the Facultad de Matemáticas of UCM in the early 1980s and led it for several years. In 2006, he founded the Instituto de Matemática Interdisciplinar (IMI),<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.mat.ucm.es/~jidiaz/Breve_CV/Currweb.htm|title=Jesús Ildefonso DÍAZ: Short CV|date=2019-07-05|website=www.mat.ucm.es|access-date=2019-07-22}}</ref> serving as Director from 2006 to 2008 and again from 2012 to 2016. He is an energetic teacher, organizing six summer courses at UCM, two of them with Jacques Louis Lions.

Díaz has worked in many areas of [[Applied Mathematics|applied mathematics]], such as theoretical and applied aspects of [[nonlinear partial differential equation]]s, [[Fluid Mechanics|fluid mechanics]] models, [[geophysical]] models, reaction-diffusion models, [[Elasticity (physics)|elasticity]] and homogenization models and control theory models, among others. He has also worked in areas closer to [[Pure Mathematics|pure mathematics]], such as [[nonlinear analysis]], focusing on [[accretive operator]]s, rearrangement and gradient estimates. Other activities include contributions in science history, science communication and scientific management. His mentors and influential colleagues include Philippe Benilan and [[Jacques Louis Lions]].

As of July 2019, his research publications included more than 250 papers in research journals, 141 contributions published in proceedings of meetings, seven books, eight book chapters and 20 edited volumes. His popular science works include 43 articles, two memoirs, two contributions to published proceedings and 17 chapters in books.<ref name=":1" /> He has collaborated with over 175 researchers. Since 1979, he has been advisor for 20 Ph.D. dissertations (all at UCM). He has 106 scientific "descendants".<ref>{{MathGenealogy |127475}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
*2015: Grand Prix ''Jacques-Louis Lions'' de Mathématiques Appliquées of the [[Académie des Sciences]] (France).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Laureats/laureats-2015-prix-thematiques.html|title=Lauréats 2015 des prix thématiques {{!}} Lauréats {{!}} Prix et médailles {{!}} Encourager la vie scientifique|website=www.academie-sciences.fr|access-date=2019-07-22}}</ref>
*1997: Member of the [[Spanish Royal Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.rac.es/2/2_ficha.php?id=63&idN3=6&idN4=40|title=Real Academia de Ciencias Exactas, Físicas y Naturales - Académicos - Numerarios|website=www.rac.es|access-date=2019-02-28|archive-date=2015-12-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222092520/http://www.rac.es/2/2_ficha.php?id=63&idN3=6&idN4=40|url-status=dead}}</ref>
*1996: Doctorate "Honoris Causa" from the [[University of Pau and Pays de l'Adour]].<ref name=":0" />
*1980: Mathematics Prize of the [[Real Academia de Ciencias Exactas, Físicas y Naturales|Spanish Royal Academy of Sciences]], 1980.<ref name=":1" />

== Congresses and scientific academies ==
Díaz was instrumental in the organization of the Spanish Congress of Differential Equations and Applications, an annual national meeting held from 1978 to 1987.  This meeting catalyzed discussions in 1988 on the need for a national society.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www-groups.dcs.st-and.ac.uk/~history/Societies/Spanish_Applied.html|title=Spanish Society of Applied Mathematics|website=www-groups.dcs.st-and.ac.uk|access-date=2019-07-23}}</ref> With Antonio Valle ([[University of Málaga]]), Díaz co-founded the [[:es:Sociedad Española de Matemática Aplicada|Sociedad Española de Matemática Aplicada]] (SEMA), serving as the society's Secretary from its founding in 1991 to 1994, and as its second President, after Valle, from 1994 to 1995.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sema.org.es/es/sociedad-3/objetivos-e-historia-2|title=SEMA - Objetivos e historia|website=www.sema.org.es|access-date=2019-07-23}}</ref>

He was influential in the reformation of the Spanish Royal Society of Mathematics in 1997, after it had been inactive for several years.<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|last1=Casal|first1=A.C.|last2=Rakotoson|first2=J.-M.|date=2011|title=Dedication to Professor Jesus Ildefonso Diaz on the occasion of his 60th birthday|url=https://www.rsme.es/arbolmat/IldefonsoDiaz/2011-Casal-Rakotoson--Dedication-JID-60th.pdf|journal=Differential Equations and Applications.|volume=3|issue=4 |pages=463–467|doi=10.7153/dea-03-29 }}</ref> As a member of the Spanish Royal Academy of Sciences, he worked to modernize the academy's activities. He was the founder of the mathematics section of the [[RACSAM|''Journal of the Spanish Royal Academy of Sciences, Series A Mathematics'' (RACSAM)]], serving as editor-in-chief from 2001 to 2005. He encouraged links between the academy and the [[French Academy of Sciences]], co-organizing a joint congress "Les Mathématiques et l'environnement", held in Paris.<ref name=":2" />

He is responsible for the fact that the word ''modelizar'' was accepted by the [[Real Academia Española|Royal Academy of the Spanish Language]] and included in the Spanish Official Dictionary as the correct Spanish translation for the English word ''modelling''.

== International relationships ==
As a result of his activities to connect Spanish and French mathematicians, he was appointed to visiting positions in many French universities, including the Universities of Toulouse, Nancy, Pau, Metz, Tours, Poitiers, Paris VI and Montpellier. He organized several French-Spanish congresses on various topics.<ref name=":2" />

He has also been appointed as an honorary member of the Mathematics Research Center, [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]], USA, and Visiting Professor at the [[University of Rome II]] and the [[University of L'Aquila]]). He organized the [[NATO]] Advanced Study Institute on the Mathematics of Models for Climatology and Environment in 1995.<ref name=":2" />

From 2009 to 2013 he was European Coordinator of the European Programme FIRST (Fronts and Interfaces in Science and Technologies), with a €4 million budget and activities in 11 countries.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mat.ucm.es/~FIRST/|title=Fronts and Interfaces in Science and Technology|website=www.mat.ucm.es|access-date=2019-07-23}}</ref>

== Editorial boards ==
From September 2003 to June 2014 he was the only Spanish person on the editorial board of the Journal of the European Mathematical Society. He serves on the editorial boards of several other journals including:

* Advances in Mathematical Science and Applications (since 1991)
* Revista de la Real Academia de Ciencias Exactas, Físicas y Naturales de Madrid (since 1996)
* Electronic Differential Equations Journal (since 2001).
* Differential and Integral Equations (since 2001).
* Electronic Journal of Mathematical and Physical Sciences (since 2002).
* [[Journal of the European Mathematical Society]] (since 2003).
* The Annals of the University of Craiova - Mathematics and Computer Science (since 2006).
* Nonlinear Analysis: Real World Applications (since 2010).
* Differential Equations and Applications (DEA) (since 2011).
* Abstract and Applied Analysis (since July 2012).

== 60th birthday celebration ==
An International Congress was organized to celebrate Díaz's 60th birthday, entitled "Non-linear models in partial differential equations: A conference on the occasion of Jesús Ildefonso Díaz's 60th birthday".<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.mat.ucm.es/~homenajeJIDiaz60/|title=Conference in honour of Jesus Ildefonso Díaz|website=www.mat.ucm.es|access-date=2019-02-28}}</ref> The meeting took place on June, 14-17, 2011, in the Palacio de Lorenzana, (UCLM) in Toledo, Spain (Ildefonso's birthplace). The members of the Scientific Committee were Professors Haïm Brezis (President), H. Ammann, S.N. Antontsev, [[Avner Friedman|A. Friedman]], R. Glowinski, A. Liñán, E. Sánchez-Palencia, and [[Roger Meyer Temam|R. Temam]]. Two special issues of the journal ''Differential Equations and Applications'' were dedicated to the meeting proceedings (''Differential Equations and Applications'' Vol. 3, Issue 4 (2011) and Vol. 4 Issue 1 (2012)). {{ISSN|1847-120X}}.
